title: ECB Raises Key Rates by 25 Basis Points as Middle East Conflict Sustains Inflationary Pressures
intro: The European Central Bank's Governing Council voted on September 10, 2026 to raise its three key interest rates by 25 basis points, citing persistent inflationary dynamics driven in part by the ongoing Middle East conflict. The decision reinforces the institution's commitment to anchoring inflation at its 2% medium-term target, even as the growth outlook for the euro area faces notable downside risks. The move brings the deposit facility rate to 2.50%, the main refinancing operations rate to 2.65%, and the marginal lending facility rate to 2.90%, effective September 16, 2026.

sections.heading: Rate Decision and Policy Rationale
sections.content: The Governing Council's decision to tighten monetary conditions by an additional 25 basis points reflects the continued assessment that inflation will remain materially above target for a prolonged period. The Middle East conflict has emerged as a key exogenous driver of inflationary pressures, sustaining uncertainty across energy markets and complicating the ECB's baseline forecasting assumptions. In this context, the rate adjustment underscores the Governing Council's resolve to pursue price stability without accommodation, maintaining a data-dependent posture that avoids any pre-commitment to a specific rate trajectory. Decisions will continue to be taken on a meeting-by-meeting basis, evaluated against incoming economic and financial data, underlying inflation dynamics, and the effective transmission of monetary policy across the euro area. The Transmission Protection Instrument remains available to counter unwarranted and disorderly market dynamics that could impair the uniform transmission of monetary policy across member states.

sections.heading: Updated Macroeconomic Projections: Inflation Revised Higher, Growth More Resilient Than Expected
sections.content: ECB staff projections released alongside the September decision present a nuanced macroeconomic picture. Headline inflation is projected to average 3.0% in 2026, declining to 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028. Core inflation, excluding energy and food components, is forecast at 2.5% in 2026, 2.6% in 2027, and 2.3% in 2028. Notably, inflation projections for 2027 and 2028 have been revised upward relative to the June 2026 exercise, while the 2026 estimate remains unchanged. This upward revision signals that second-round effects and indirect pass-through from the energy shock may be proving more persistent than previously modelled. On the growth side, the euro area economy is projected to expand by 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027, and 1.5% in 2028. The upward revision to the 2026 and 2027 growth estimates reflects greater-than-expected economic resilience, suggesting that domestic demand and labour market dynamics have provided a degree of insulation against the external shock environment.

sections.heading: Uncertainty Landscape and Balance Sheet Normalization
sections.content: The Governing Council acknowledges that the macroeconomic outlook remains subject to a high degree of uncertainty, with risks skewed to the upside for inflation and to the downside for growth — a configuration that complicates the conventional monetary policy trade-off. ECB experts have developed alternative scenarios to capture the wide range of potential outcomes depending on the intensity, duration, and second-round effects of the energy shock stemming from the Middle East conflict. In parallel, balance sheet normalization continues at a measured and predictable pace. The Asset Purchase Programme and the Pandemic Emergency Purchase Programme portfolios are declining as the Eurosystem refrains from reinvesting principal payments on maturing securities. The Governing Council retains full flexibility to deploy all instruments within its mandate should conditions warrant, including those designed to preserve the orderly functioning of monetary policy transmission mechanisms across the euro area.

quote: Headline inflation is projected at 3.0% in 2026, with core inflation at 2.5% — both materially above the ECB's 2% medium-term target, as upward revisions to 2027 and 2028 forecasts signal persistent underlying price pressures.
conclusion: The September 2026 ECB rate decision illustrates a central bank navigating a difficult equilibrium: combating above-target inflation driven by an external geopolitical shock while managing increasingly tangible downside risks to growth. With deposit rates now at 2.50% and projections indicating that headline inflation will not converge to the 2% objective until 2028 at the earliest, the Governing Council's data-dependent approach leaves the door open to further tightening should price dynamics deteriorate. Markets and institutional investors should closely monitor the ECB President's press conference, energy market developments, and any evolution in conflict-related supply disruptions, as these will be the primary variables shaping the pace and terminal level of the current tightening cycle. Flexibility, vigilance, and data sensitivity remain the defining hallmarks of ECB policy at this juncture.
excerpt: ECB raises rates by 25bps to 2.50% on deposits as Middle East conflict sustains inflation well above the 2% target through 2028.
